acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

data.reason: Diane, the CFO, froze all new vendor projects after a missed Q3. Finance saw billing as a 'nice to have'. Renee blames timing, but Owen never got the payback number he asked for.

trigger.action: Lead with how long one pricing change takes on homegrown billing.
trigger.why: Pikeview's billing was built by someone who left, and Owen said every pricing change took a quarter.
trigger.quote: every pricing change takes them a quarter

decider.action: Tell finance what homegrown billing costs them, not what engineers gain.
decider.why: Diane, the CFO, was never in a meeting. Our story only reached product and engineering.
decider.quote: Owen said finance saw it as a nice to have.

competitor.action: Spell out the cost of doing nothing: lapsed renewals, errors, engineering time.
competitor.why: With no other vendor in play, Owen's late questions turned to payback, so doing nothing was the rival.
competitor.quote: do you have something that shows payback?

message.action: Swap 'grow revenue' for roadmap time saved when selling billing.
message.why: Owen rejected the revenue pitch but loved seeing a price changed in a few clicks.
message.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing

proof.action: Add a payback example built from one customer's own billing costs.
proof.why: Renee sent Owen the general ROI deck, and he said it would not convince Diane.
proof.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

words.action: Describe homegrown billing as 'a tax on the roadmap'.
words.why: Owen used this phrase for his problem, and it was the reason he wanted to rebuild.
